searches.reason: Explore a time-aware GRU that learns when to retain durable preferences and when to reset toward recent activity. This moves beyond fixed recency weights while preserving one jointly trained GRU4Rec per category. Seek affordable implementations using observed training timestamps, with ablations separating elapsed time from sequence position; timestamps alone cannot establish current intent.

searches.reason: Investigate whether jointly learned title and description features help distinguish specific products and experiences where item-ID recurrence captures only broad affinity. Seek lightweight text encoders trained from scratch inside the GRU4Rec network, without pretrained weights or separate score fusion. Evaluate whether gains extend beyond frequent items; text similarity alone does not establish compatibility or complementary value.

searches.reason: Challenge the assumption that harder negatives alone resolve Electronics’ weak sampled separation. Seek sequence-level self-supervision that improves context discrimination within the same GRU network, using order-preserving views and explicit false-negative handling. Compare against a fixed BPR-max control and inspect score norms and history dependence; mean embedding alignment does not itself establish collapse.
